alternate.quote: The northern mass peak in the Subaru mass map is further resolved into two peaks thanks to the factor of two increase in the {\it HST} source density. ... uncertainty_related_text.quote: The centroids of P2 and P4 between the two mass reconstructions agree within $\mytilde0\farcm2$, which is expected from the noise level of the Subaru-only result. ... when we smooth the mass map from the HST-Subaru joint analysis, the centroid of the merged mass peak differs from that of the Subaru-only version by $\mytilde0\farcm5$, which is again consistent with the noise\footnote{We estimate the centroid errors by utilizing the publicly available {\tt FIATMAP} code (Fischer \& Tyson 1997), ...}.
uncertainty_related_text.comment: Centroid errors are said to be estimated (FIATMAP) but no numerical 1-sigma value is reported.

notes: Paper match: arXiv 1510.03486 = Jee et al. 2016 ApJ 817, 179 (DOI 10.3847/0004-637X/817/2/179). Pointer: Table 2 (tablenum 2) is the substructure table with P1-P4 centroids - matches; 'Two-dimensional Mass Distribution' is §4.3 in the arXiv source (sections: 1 Intro, 2 Observations, 3 WL Method, 4 WL Results, 5 Discussion, 6 Conclusions), so pointer §3.3 is off by one section (published numbering may differ); Fig. 6 = joint HST+Subaru mass map (fig_hst_subaru_massmap) - matches; Fig. 8 = mass vs X-ray comparison. Only x_I has absolute coordinates (P1; P3 also northern). No positional uncertainty is given for any mass peak (Table 2 gives significance only). x_G: only an approximate offset '~0.5 arcmin' between the northern mass peak and the northern X-ray peak. x_S: no coordinates for luminosity peaks or BCG; only qualitative 'coincides with the galaxy luminosity peak' (no number). Other positions in paper (not relevant): bright star at (6:03:17.5, 42:12:25) 'between the two X-ray peaks'. Redshift used for kpc: 0.225.
